newsitem.title: USA: Mark IV sells two units for $35.5 million.
newsitem.headline: Mark IV sells two units for $35.5 million.

text.p: Mark IV Industries Inc. said Thursday it sold two of its non-core units, Gulton Data Systems and LFE Industrial Systems, for about $35.5 million.

Gulton, based in Albuquerque, N.M., was sold to BFGoodrich Co. of Richfield, Ohio, for about $23 million. Gulton makes data acquisition systems for satellites and other aerospace applications. It had about $25 million in revenues for the fiscal year ended Feb. 28.

LFE, based in Clinton, Mass., was sold to Eurotherm Plc, of Worthing, England, for $12.5 million. LFE makes computer-based measurement and control systems. It had revenues of about $9.5 million in fiscal 1997.

Mark IV said the two units were among several non-core businesses it recently sold in order to focus on making power transmission, fluid transfer and filtration systems and components for global industrial and automotive markets.
Mark IV said the sales bring total proceeds from the Amherst, N.Y.-based company's divestiture programme to about $313 million, most of which was realised during fiscal 1997.

BFGoodrich provides aircraft systems and services, and manufactures speciality chemicals. Eurotherm Plc is engaged in the design, manufacture and sale of automation equipment for industrial process industries.
Mark IV's stock rose 50 cents to $23.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
